prompt: About how many degrees is $1$ radian?
hint: Start from $\pi$ radians $= 180^\circ$ and divide both sides by $\pi$.

hints.text: Start from $\pi$ radians $= 180^\circ$ and divide both sides by $\pi$.

explanation: Since $\pi$ radians $= 180^\circ$, dividing both sides by $\pi$ gives $1$ radian $= \frac{180^\circ}{\pi}$.
It is worth memorizing: a radian is a bit under $60^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count radians around a circle
steps: A full circle is $2\pi \approx 6.28$ radians and also $360^\circ$.
So one radian is $\frac{360^\circ}{6.28} \approx 57.3^\circ$ — a circle holds a little more than 6 radians.
